name: MIME Type Lookup
description: Find the MIME media type of a file extension, or find the usual extensions of a media type.

hints.query: Write an extension (png, .png, report.pdf), a media type (image/png) or a keyword; parameters such as text/plain; charset=utf-8 are stripped automatically. The search and the top-level type filter combine.
hints.output: Every media type is listed by default; typing a search term or picking a top-level type narrows the list instantly, showing media type / extensions / top-level type / charset / description, each row copyable.
hints.note: Data comes from a built-in snapshot; the system MIME database is never read and nothing is fetched from the network.

faq.a: Office 2007 switched to the Open XML format, so .docx is application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document; application/msword describes the older .doc format.

faq.q: Can one extension have several media types?
faq.a: Yes: .xml is described both as application/xml and as text/xml. The tool returns the more common one and keeps the other as a separate entry, which is still reachable by looking the media type up directly.

faq.q: Why is the charset sometimes empty?
faq.a: A charset only makes sense for textual types. Images, archives and fonts have no default charset, so the field stays empty.
